answer: A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 154 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The terrace detector writes to delta, and reef shows every merge. Submissions that land within 221 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 38 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
